This is found at `HEAD@{1}` in the reflog, labeled **"commit: Third note - contains bug fix"**.

# Recovering a Deleted Branch via Git Reflog

## Reading the Reflog (Bottom → Top)

```
Timeline of events:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
HEAD@{5}: commit (initial): Initial project setup          ← started repo
HEAD@{4}: checkout: moving from main to feature-login      ← created branch
HEAD@{3}: commit: Add auth module                          ← 1st feature commit
HEAD@{2}: commit: Add login function - critical feature    ← ✅ TARGET COMMIT
HEAD@{1}: checkout: moving from feature-login to main      ← switched back
HEAD@{0}: merge feature-login: Fast-forward                ← merged & deleted
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

## Identifying the Target Commit

The commit containing **"critical feature"** is at `HEAD@{2}`:

```
00594a29... HEAD@{2}: commit: Add login function - critical feature
```

## Recovery Command

Recreate the deleted branch pointing to that exact commit:

```bash
# Using the commit hash
git branch feature-login 00594a29e0494044ed99986d89e4ecfa67517f79

# OR using the reflog shorthand
git branch feature-login HEAD@{2}
```

To recover **and** switch to it in one step:

```bash
git checkout -b feature-login 00594a29
```

## Verify the Recovery

```bash
# Confirm the branch exists again
git branch
#   * main
#     feature-login

# Confirm it points to the right commit
git log feature-login --oneline
#   00594a2 Add login function - critical feature
#   28e4ced Add auth module
#   336bfd0 Initial project setup
```

## Key Takeaway

```
Deleted branch ≠ Deleted commits
│
├── Git keeps commits in reflog for ~90 days
├── Reflog tracks every HEAD movement (commits, checkouts, merges)
└── As long as you have the commit hash, you can always recover
```

> **Note:** In this case the merge was a **fast-forward**, so `main` already points to the same commit (`00594a29`). But recreating the branch is still useful if you need to continue development on `feature-login` separately.
